data.narrative:
Kipu Quantum is a seed-stage quantum computing company that has raised approximately $14.5M to date. The quantum computing sector includes 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology given data constraints. The stage-progression method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, using the $14.5M raised as a value proxy. This yields an implied valuation of $36M. A peer-median approach is not applicable: while 8 quantum computing companies exist in the broader comp set, none meet narrow same-stage or adjacent-stage filters with sufficient sample size (minimum 3 required), making sector-wide median comparison unreliable and potentially misleading.

The triangulated valuation range is $31M to $42M, with a median estimate of $36M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties center on the thin methodological foundation—only one quantitative approach is defensible with available data. A peer-median analysis would strengthen conviction once same-stage or clearly comparable private quantum companies achieve sufficient density in valuation databases. The 2.5x multiplier assumption itself carries execution risk inherent to seed-stage companies.
